title: Trump tells America the economy is strong, blames Biden for nation's struggles
summary: Presidential address claiming inherited record inflation has been stopped, prices and gasoline are down, wages outpace inflation, and tariffs are funding a factory boom.

assertions.quote: When I took office, inflation was the worst in 48 years.

verdicts.note: CPI inflation was 3.0% in January 2025; the 40-year peak was 9.1% in June 2022.

The 12-month CPI change was 3.0% in January 2025, down from the 9.1% peak of June 2022 and below every reading from April 2021 to October 2023; the multi-decade high was in mid-2022, two and a half years earlier.

assertions.quote: I am bringing those high prices down and bringing them down very fast.

verdicts.note: CPI rose about 2.7-3% year over year through 2025; some items like eggs fell but the overall price level kept rising.

The NSA CPI-U rose from 317.671 in January 2025 to 324.054 in December 2025 (+2.0%), with 12-month inflation of 2.7% in November and December 2025; the level was rising, not falling, even though December's unadjusted monthly change rounded to -0.0%.

assertions.quote: inflation is stopped, wages are up, prices are down

verdicts.note: CPI inflation ran near 3% in late 2025, above the Fed's 2% target.
CPI-U rose 2.7% in the 12 months to December 2025 (seasonally adjusted monthly change +0.3%), so the US had inflation of close to 3%, not none.

assertions.quote: Gasoline is now under $2.50 a gallon. in much of the country.

verdicts.note: The national average near $3 in December 2025 was below the previous term's average, though under $2.50 held only in a few states.

December 2025 regular gasoline was 2.894, 16.4% below the Biden-period mean of 3.461 and 41.3% below the Biden peak of 4.929; only 3 of the 48 Biden months (Feb-Apr 2021: 2.501, 2.810, 2.858) were lower.

assertions.quote: for the first time in years, wages are rising much faster than inflation

verdicts.note: Real average hourly earnings for all employees fell 0.7% from September 2025 to September 2026 (nominal pay +3.0% vs CPI +3.7%), so the typical worker's purchasing power declined over the past year rather than rose.

assertions.quote: I've secured a record-breaking $18 trillion of investment into the United States

verdicts.note: BEA recorded foreign direct investment of a few hundred billion in 2025 and trackers found roughly $600 billion of announced capital spending; the trillions are unverified pledges.

assertions.quote: They're building factories and plants at levels we haven't seen.

verdicts.note: Manufacturing employment fell through 2025-26 and manufacturing construction spending declined from its 2024 peak.

assertions.quote: The price of eggs is down 82% since March. And everything else is falling rapidly.

verdicts.note: Food-at-home CPI rose about 2-3% in 2025; eggs fell sharply from a bird-flu peak but beef, coffee and other staples rose.

The CPI food index rose from 335.517 in January 2025 to 343.795 in December 2025 (+2.5%), with 12-month food inflation of 3.1% in December 2025; the series covers all food (including food away from home) rather than groceries alone, hence the slightly lower confidence.
